brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 kids' evites starring Plajah's own kaiju mascots, Chora (music note on the belly, purple goggle markings) and Reello (camera, orange goggle markings). Decide the 12 scenarios, how the mascots perform inside the invite (they can be animated 2D puppets or the rigged 3D models), and how a guest's tap or game makes them react.
brief.audience: Kids and parents; also brand-building for Plajah itself.
brief.feeling: Our characters, our world: mischievous, warm, unmistakably Plajah.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.
The mascots must stay on-model (wide mochi head, white face, chevron cap with navy gem, goggle patches, angular magenta/orange ruff, cat-ear horns).
references: Exploration grid A: Chora and Reello at a birthday party, one holding a frosted cake with candles, the other with a party horn, balloons and string lights, confetti; on-model, polished 3D.
Exploration grid B: the two dancing on a light-up disco floor under a mirror ball; on-model, energetic.

proposals.title: Canon, Measure, Mascot, Feast
proposals.idea: Each invite is a ruled illuminated page — a single governing proportion (the golden section, redrawn as a living grid) holds every element in counterpoint, so Chora and Reello perform like voices in a two-part invention: their gestures answer each other across a structural axis that never breaks, no matter the scenario.
proposals.geometry: A golden-section rectangle (1 : 1.618) anchors the full card. A horizontal rule at the φ division — approximately 241 px from the top of a 390 px-wide canvas — acts as the 'cantus firmus': the mascots always straddle or bracket this line; text lives below it in a five-column grid derived from the same ratio. No element is placed arbitrarily; every margin is a sub-division of the governing measure. Across all 12 cards the grid is identical; only what inhabits it changes — the same way a sonata form carries twelve different movements.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Freight Display Pro (Italic) — classical weight, ink-trap serifs that read as engraved without pastiche. Event title set at 44 px / leading 48 px, tracked −10, small caps for the venue line. Secondary: Söhne Mono for date and time — the monospaced column recalls a concert programme's running order, giving parents the data legibility they need. All live Tela text; no type baked into art plates. Hierarchy: display → mono data → body (Freight Text Pro Regular, 14 px). Nothing is centred arbitrarily; alignment follows the five-column grid.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographic backgrounds. The art plate is an original gouache-and-ink wash — painted on 300 gsm hot-press, photographed under raking daylight so the paper tooth reads — then composited as a muted tonal field behind the mascots. The wash colour shifts per scenario (deep prussian for the disco card; warm ochre for the outdoor picnic card) but the paper texture is always present as a reminder of the hand. The mascots are rigged 3D models rendered against transparency, dropped onto the wash as foreground cut-outs. They do not merge with the background; they inhabit it the way a soloist inhabits a stage.
proposals.texture: The art plate carries visible brushstroke and paper tooth (photographed physical material — this is the human trace). The WebGL foil-shimmer mask is applied only along the cantus firmus rule and the gem on the chevron cap, so shimmer has structural purpose rather than decorating everything. Candle-flicker particles (on the birthday card) are confined to a rectangular lantern-shaped mask derived from the grid, not scattered freely. Bokeh is suppressed; I concede to The Radical Minimalist here — bokeh without a focal logic is decoration, not depth.
proposals.motion: Sequence is governed by a three-beat rhythmic arc — the same pacing logic as a classical rondo: A (entry), B (event), A′ (resolution). On card load: the gouache wash fades up over 600 ms (ease-in, no bounce). At 620 ms the cantus firmus rule draws itself left-to-right over 400 ms — a single horizontal ink stroke, WebGL-drawn, giving the page its spine before anything else appears. At 1 100 ms the mascots rise from below the rule into their positions over 500 ms (spring with critical damping — no overshoot). On phone tilt: the foreground mascot layer parallaxes at 0.4× the tilt vector; the wash layer at 0.15× — two distinct depths, no more, preserving readable hierarchy. Tap gesture triggers the scenario-specific reaction (see below). On reduced-motion: the rule appears instantly, mascots appear at rest, no parallax, no draw animation — full legibility preserved.
proposals.productionMethod: 12 gouache-and-ink washes painted by a single illustrator on identical 300 gsm Fabriano Artistico sheets, photographed under consistent north-facing daylight (same lamp angle, same camera height) so the texture reads as a series — like pages of a manuscript. Mascots: rigged 3D models exported as transparent WebP sprite sheets per scenario. Grid and rule: SVG, drawn by algorithm from the φ ratio, embedded in Tela. WebGL effects layer built in Tela's shader pipeline with shimmer confined to structural masks. Live text tokens (name, date, venue) injected by Tela at render time. QR and link-preview thumbnail crops to the zone above the cantus firmus rule, always showing both mascots — compositional consequence built into the proportion from the start.
proposals.humanTrace: The gouache wash on photographed hot-press paper — brushstroke direction, tide lines at wash edges, and paper tooth are all visible at 390 px. The raking-light photograph is the document of making. This is not a simulated texture; it is a scanned physical object.
proposals.risk: The governing grid and the classical type may read as 'formal' or 'adult' to a buyer expecting something looser. The risk is worth it because: (a) the mascots' mochi warmth and the scenario energy supply the playfulness — the structure is the container that makes their mischief legible rather than chaotic; (b) at brand-building scale, a card that has a recognisable geometry across 12 variants builds Plajah's design authority rather than blending into the saturated evite market. The measure is what makes the series a series.

arguesWith.why: The Rebellious Hand will call the golden-section grid a cage that domesticates Chora and Reello's energy, and will want the mascots to break frame, spill over edges, refuse the rule. I hold that a mark with no structure behind it is noise with confidence — the φ division is not a cage, it is the thing that makes the mascots' position on the page mean something. proposals.title: Ink Pressed, Kaiju Loose
proposals.idea: Each invite begins as a photographed relief print — Chora and Reello stamped in imperfect layers of ink on real paper — then the 2D puppet rigs tear free from the print's outline and animate over it, so the digital character literally escapes its own physical origin.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile slab. The print plate occupies the full bleed as the art layer — no safe white border. Mascots are off-axis, 7–10 degrees tilted, never centred: Chora leans into the upper-left third, Reello anchors lower-right. Text sits on a narrow torn-tape horizontal band crossing the mid-third, keeping it legible at 390px without competing with the characters. The twelve scenarios are differentiated by the shape of the torn band, not by layout grid changes.
proposals.typography: Degular Display (bold, 28–36px, mixed case, tight tracking –20) for the party headline — its blunt ink-trap corners echo letterpress. Mono45 Headline (regular, 13px, all-caps, +80 tracking) for date/time/venue in the tape band. No script, no rounded bubble fonts — those are what the user references already have and what the Baroque direction will reach for. The type should look like it was stamped, not set.
proposals.imageLogic: The base art plate is a photographed linocut or woodblock print — hand-carved silhouettes of each scenario's setting (jungle gym, cinema, skate bowl, etc.) in two-colour reduction print, shot on a flatbed scanner at 1200dpi. Chora and Reello's puppet rigs are vector/2D animation overlaid on top: they sit inside the printed silhouette outlines at rest, then on tap they 'escape' — the rig slides, bounces, and rotates out of the carved shape, leaving an ink ghost behind. No photographic portraits of real people; all imagery is original Plajah asset or the hand-printed plate.
proposals.texture: The scanned linocut plate is the ground. Its ink drag marks, uneven pressure spots, and plate-edge shadow are preserved and treated as signal, not noise. A WebGL foil shimmer is masked strictly to the inked areas — it only appears where ink physically pressed paper, so the sheen is earned by the dent. The torn-tape text band is a photographed strip of kraft packing tape, scanned, placed as the live-text mask so the words appear to be written on real tape.
proposals.motion: On load: the scanned plate fades in first — 0.4s, no easing flourish, just a straight cut — so the physical object is seen before the digital character appears. Then Chora and Reello puppet-rigs blink into existence inside their ink outlines (0.6s). Idle: they breathe — a 2s loop of subtle chest rise and goggle-patch blink, staying inside the print shape. On tap: the mascots burst out of the outline in the direction of the tap, bounce once off the phone edge (tilt sensor), then land in a new position with a fresh ink-splat particle that uses the plate's actual ink colour. Foil shimmer pulses only on the ink areas during the burst. Reduced-motion mode: tap triggers a single static 'escaped' pose swap — no bounce, no particle — print plate fades slightly to make room. Candle flicker WebGL reserved for the birthday scenario only, masked to the printed candle silhouettes.
proposals.productionMethod: Physical: carve one reduction linocut per scenario (12 plates, each 200×300mm) using Pfeil gouges; print two-colour on 120gsm uncoated stock; flatbed scan at 1200dpi. Digital: clean the scan in Photoshop — remove dust, keep ink texture and pressure variance. Import into Tela as the generated art plate layer. Build Chora and Reello as 2D rigged puppets in a rig tool (After Effects puppet pins or Rive), export as Rive WASM for the foreground cut-out layer. WebGL foil mask is painted by tracing the ink areas from the scan using a pressure-sensitive tablet — the mask shape is itself a human gesture. Live text layer in Tela holds names, dates, venues.
proposals.humanTrace: The linocut plate's ink drag, gouge-cut edges, and pressure variation are photographically preserved and visible in the final invite at full zoom. The WebGL foil mask is a hand-traced gesture over the ink, made with a stylus. The Chora/Reello puppet escape-burst leaves an ink-splat particle drawn from the actual scanned ink bleed — it is not a procedural circle; it is a digitised ink mark.
proposals.risk: Parents and brand stakeholders may read 'linocut texture' as low-budget or craft-fair rather than jaw-dropping. The risk is worth it because the physical origin is legible — you can see the tool marks — and that specificity is exactly what differentiates this from the smooth 3D party references the user already has. The print says someone made this for your kid. The Futurist will say the linocut is nostalgia performance and that the rig-escape concept is the only interesting part. I say the rig escape only means something if there is a real physical thing to escape from.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist will want to strip the linocut plate and replace it with a procedurally generated environment — particle fields, real-time shader backgrounds — arguing the physical scan is a costume over a digital system. I disagree specifically because the escape-from-print narrative collapses without the print. If the mascots burst out of a procedural field, they are just bouncing inside a simulati

proposals.title: Field Notebooks From Kaiju Country
proposals.idea: Each invite is a page torn from a naturalist's field notebook — a different real documentary-photography biome per scenario — where Chora and Reello have been spotted, annotated, and pinned like newly discovered species, so every party type gets its own specific geography instead of a generic festive backdrop.
proposals.geometry: Portrait A5 field-notebook page (390 × 690 px safe zone), ruled with faint 1.5 mm pencil lines that are photographed from an actual Leuchtturm notebook and composited as a texture layer; a torn-edge bleed at the bottom third separates the 'field observation zone' (top, kaiju) from the 'specimen data zone' (bottom, live text: name, date, venue); a single hand-drawn circle annotation ring — scanned ink, not vector — encircles the mascot group as a field-ID marker; no symmetry axis, deliberate left-lean to feel discovered rather than designed
proposals.typography: Headlines: Recia (or fallback: Playfair Display Italic) in 13 pt, letterspaced +80, ALL CAPS, mimicking rubber-stamp field classification — stamped in a slightly rotated 2–3° tilt per card, never perfectly level; body / live text block: iA Writer Quattro (monospace reading feel) at 11 pt, flush-left, 1.6 line-height, in deep ink-brown #2B1A0E; a second script layer — the biome name only — hand-lettered by a single human calligrapher, photographed, masked to white paper, placed at top-left as a genuine artifact; no display sans anywhere
proposals.imageLogic: Each of the 12 scenarios maps to a specific, named, licensable documentary-photography biome: e.g. Scenario 1 (birthday) = night market, Chiang Rai, Thailand, 2019 (Getty RF #1234567 or equivalent with full credit); Scenario 2 (pool party) = Algarve tide-pool, Portugal; Scenario 3 (movie night) = drive-in, Tulsa Oklahoma 1970s archival; Scenario 4 (disco) = Lagos Afrobeats club, 2022 — all photographs are desaturated to a warm-cream duotone (shadow: #2B1A0E, highlight: #F5EDD8) so they read as field-notebook wash, then the mascots are composited on top as the only full-colour elements, creating a figure-ground hierarchy that is unmistakable at 390 px; no AI-generated landscapes; every photograph credit lives in 7 pt iA Quattro below the torn edge
proposals.texture: Base plate is a high-res scan of actual cream Fabriano field-paper (300 dpi, photographed under raking side-light to show chain-lines and laid-lines); pencil-rule lines are a second scan layer at 40% opacity; the WebGL foil layer is gated exclusively by the ink-bleed halos of the scanned annotation ring — so shimmer only appears inside the hand-drawn circle, honouring the physical tool-mark; a micro-grain noise overlay (SVG feTurbulence, seed per card) prevents any card feeling digitally smooth
proposals.motion: On load (0–0.4 s): the duotone photograph fades up like a darkroom print emerging — slow, bottom to top; (0.4–0.8 s): the scanned paper texture settles in with a subtle curl-flatten ease; (0.8–1.2 s): Chora and Reello 2D-puppet-rig drift into frame from off-left, as if the naturalist just spotted them — they wobble on landing with a single 4-frame secondary bounce; (1.2–2 s): the ink annotation ring draws itself around them in real time (SVG stroke-dashoffset animation, 600 ms ease-in-out); on phone tilt: the mascot foreground layer parallaxes ±8 px against the paper background, the bokeh/particle layer (floating field-notebook detritus: pressed-leaf shapes, ink-drop bokeh) moves ±16 px in the opposite direction; tap on mascots: Chora plays a 12-frame music-note burst from her belly, Reello clicks his camera shutter — a white-flash light-leak (WebGL) bleeds outward from the annotation ri
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: art director scouts 12 specific licensed documentary photographs, one per scenario, and logs provenance in a shared Tela asset registry with photographer credit and license number. Step 2: a human calligrapher letters 12 biome names (one per card) on cream paper; these are photographed at 1200 dpi and masked. Step 3: Fabriano paper and Leuchtturm notebook pages are scanned; pencil-rule and chain-line textures are extracted as multiply-blend PNG tiles. Step 4: Chora and Reello 2D puppet rigs (built in the Tela rig system from the approved on-model vector assets) are exported as layered transparent foreground cut-outs per scenario pose — no 3D render here, deliberate choice. Step 5: the annotation ring is hand-drawn in Rotring ink on each card's paper scan, then scanned and SVG-traced for stroke-dashoffset animation. Step 6: WebGL foil/shimmer mask is derived algorithmically from t
proposals.humanTrace: The scanned Rotring ink annotation ring: its irregular pressure variation, the slight ink-pool at the start of the stroke, and the chain-lines of the Fabriano paper showing through it are all perceptible at 2× zoom — no element of this ring is vector-smooth; the calligrapher's biome name carries visible nib pressure variation; the photograph's darkroom-emergence animation is paced to the actual developing speed of a fibre-base print (≈35 s real time, compressed to 0.4 s but preserving the bottom-to-top directionality that any darkroom worker would recognise)
proposals.risk: Parents who open a child's birthday invite expecting balloons may be briefly disoriented by a desaturated landscape photograph of a Thai night market — the payoff is that each card feels genuinely specific and memorable rather than generically festive, and Plajah builds a world with real geographic texture rather than a fantasy nowhere; the risk is worth it because the mascots in full colour against the duotone ground are immediately warm and character-forward, and the annotation ring makes it legible as celebration within 0.8 seconds

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will argue that the field-notebook texture, the scanned paper, the calligraphy layer, and the documentary photograph are four competing surfaces too many — they will call for stripping to one ground and one figure. I refuse that reduction here: the layers are not decoration, they are provenance-carriers; removing the photograph removes the geographic specificity that makes each of t

proposals.title: Kaiju Opera: Twelve Curtain Rises
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature proscenium — a single breathtaking reveal timed to the guest's tap, where Chora and Reello erupt from darkness into sculpted theatrical light, making every birthday, recital, and sleepover feel like opening night at a kaiju opera house.
proposals.geometry: A tall portrait stage: 390px wide, no bleed wasted. The lower third is a deep shadow sill — the 'pit' — where live text (name, date, venue) floats in engraved letterpress register. The upper two-thirds is the proscenium 'fly space': Chora and Reello occupy center mass, never cropped at the cheek or horn-tip. A hard diagonal split at roughly 58/42 separates the characters' light zones, echoing Bernini's two-source marble drama. Twelve scenarios share this skeleton but vary the wing-flat silhouettes (birthday: tiered cake architecture; disco: stacked speaker columns; underwater: kelp arches; space: ringed planet frames; etc.) so the geometry transforms expressively while the structural grammar stays legible across the series.
proposals.typography: Display: Canela Deck (Commercial Type) in a steeply tracked uppercase for scenario titles — wide-set, generous x-height, a letterform with the weight of carved stone but warmth enough for a child's eye. Subhead and date: Söhne Breit (Klim) in a single-weight medium, all caps, 13px minimum, tight tracking, always white or cream on dark field. The live Tela text layer is set in Söhne Mono for venue/time metadata — monospaced legibility at small sizes without feeling like a UI mistake. No script faces: theatrical serifs and geometric grotesks only. Scale contrast is aggressive — display runs at 2.4× the body size.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographic plates used raw. Each scenario's art plate is a composited, physically lit painted maquette: a small cardboard-and-foil theatre box (roughly A5 footprint) is constructed per scenario, lit with two practical lights (one warm, one cool), photographed on a 50mm lens, and that photograph becomes the background light study. The 3D-rigged Chora and Reello models are rendered to match the maquette's exact light direction and lens perspective, then composited. The maquette photograph is desaturated and used as the chiaroscuro underpainting — the WebGL foil shimmer layer is masked to its highlight regions only, so shimmer blooms where real light fell on real foil. This means every evite carries a photograph of a made object, not a generated void.
proposals.texture: The shadow sill is deep-relief emboss simulated via a normal-mapped WebGL layer — a tactile impression of stamped board. The proscenium wing-flats use a hand-cut paper silhouette texture (scanned at 1200dpi from actual cut paper), with torn edges visible at 1× zoom. Chora's purple goggle patches and Reello's orange patches receive a micro-prismatic foil treatment in the WebGL layer — not a global shimmer, but a tight iridescent pool that responds to phone tilt, making the goggle markings appear to be inlaid enamel. The ruff (magenta/orange) is rendered with a velvet nap normal map so it reads as fabric, not plastic. Particle systems: per-scenario — birthday uses slow-rising wax-smoke bokeh particles; disco uses hexagonal mirror-chip reflections; space uses dust-grain starfield drift.
proposals.motion: The sequence is a stage timing, not a loop. Before tap: characters are in deep shadow, only the goggle patches catch a dim rim light — a held theatrical darkness of 1.2 seconds. Tap (or page-load complete for reduced-motion users, which substitutes a single gentle exposure brightening): the proscenium floods with light from the upper-left in 0.4 seconds — a hard, fast curtain-up. Characters step 6px forward (a parallax push on the foreground layer) in 0.3 seconds on a snappy ease-out, as if physically entering the lit stage. On that same beat, the scenario's signature particle system births from the characters' bodies outward. Second tap or 3-second idle: Chora executes a single held gesture (music-note belly pulses with a ripple; Reello's camera lens iris-clicks open), then returns — a 0.8-second performance window, not a loop. The wing-flat silhouettes drift on phone-tilt at 0.6× paral
proposals.productionMethod: Twelve physical maquettes built in Plajah studio — cardboard, hand-painted gouache, kitchen foil, and coloured gel film over practicals. Each photographed in one session. Chora and Reello 3D renders produced in Blender (Cycles, matched to maquette HDRI capture) per scenario; foreground cut-outs exported as transparent PNG sequences for the puppet rig states (idle, react, gesture). Tela document structure: Layer 1 — maquette photo plate (static, generated art); Layer 2 — scanned paper wing-flat silhouettes (CSS transform on tilt); Layer 3 — 3D character foreground cut-outs (parallax + tap-react states); Layer 4 — WebGL canvas (foil on goggle masks, particles, candle/bokeh per scenario); Layer 5 — live Tela text (name, date, venue, never baked). The twelve scenarios: 1-Birthday Cake Eruption, 2-Disco Mirror Ball, 3-Underwater Kelp Rave, 4-Outer Space Countdown, 5-Haunted Mansion Creep, 6-R
proposals.humanTrace: The maquette photograph — a picture of a small handmade theatre box lit by two desk lamps, its foil walls creased and slightly uneven — is embedded as the chiaroscuro underpainting in every finished evite. A child or parent who looks closely at the shadow gradients is seeing the reflection of real crumpled kitchen foil. That physical imperfection is the human trace: not gesture-painted, not procedurally generated, but a photograph of something someone built and lit by hand.
proposals.risk: The maquette production step adds real physical making time before a single pixel is designed, and it commits the series to a unified theatrical visual logic that may feel too 'adult-operatic' for the youngest audience segment. The risk is worth it because it is precisely that quality — the sense that something real and large and considered was made for you — that elevates a party evite from a template into a keepsake, and because the goggle-shimmer and curtain-up timing give children a performed moment, not a loaded asset.

I reject this entirely. A child opening an evite is not reading design criticism; they are standing at the door of

proposals.title: One Silence, One Monster
proposals.idea: Each invite is a single held breath — maximum negative space, one mascot frozen mid-gesture on a bare field, where the guest's tap or tilt is the only thing that breaks the stillness and releases the scene.
proposals.geometry: 390px column locked to a 6-unit baseline grid; mascot occupies a single asymmetric quadrant (never centered), the remaining 55–65% of the viewport left as calibrated void; a single hairline rule (0.5px, 100% viewport width) divides event text from art zone — it never moves; the 12 scenarios each rotate which quadrant the mascot inhabits (top-left, bottom-right, etc.) so the series reads as a disciplined sequence, not repetition
proposals.typography: Söhne Mono (Klim Type Foundry) for event details — mono because it quantifies time and place without decoration; set at 11px / 18px leading, tracked +80, all lowercase; a single display word naming the scenario (CAKE, DARK, DEEP, etc.) set in Söhne Breit Kräftig at 72px, 8% opacity, acting as structural field rather than headline; no drop shadows, no outlines, no gradient fills on type
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. The art plate is a flat-rendered, studio-lit kaiju on a field that reads as architect's trace paper — warm white with a barely perceptible 3% warm grain photographed from a physical sheet of Fabriano 5 pressed under glass, scanned at 1200dpi, then composited as the base layer; this is the only texture allowed and it is bound to the mechanical grid
proposals.texture: Single scanned Fabriano sheet, desaturated to near-white, compressed hard for mobile; the WebGL foil shimmer layer is masked to the mascot's goggle patches and ruff only — foil is not ambient decoration, it is reward for stillness being broken; candle flicker particle system (scenario 1 and 11 only) constrained to a 40px radius disc beneath the cake prop
proposals.motion: Default state: mascot is static, one limb in mid-gesture, held; the stillness is the invitation; on first tap — a single 0.4s ease-out breath: the mascot exhales (slight chest-scale pulse, 1.02 max scale), the foil on goggles catches light, one particle releases; tilt (gyroscope): the foreground cut-out drifts max 8px on any axis, the void field does not move — the mascot floats in fixed silence while the world barely shifts; reduced-motion flag kills all drift and particle release, substitutes a single opacity pulse (0.9 → 1.0, 600ms) on tap; nothing loops unprompted
proposals.productionMethod: Rigged 3D models exported as high-res PNG cut-outs per pose per scenario (12 hero poses, 12 reaction poses) — reaction pose is a second Tela layer that cross-dissolves on tap; Fabriano texture composited in Tela as the art plate base; WebGL shimmer and particle confined to named mask regions so Tela's live text layer sits clean above all effects; QR and link preview crops to mascot quadrant + display word only — the void is cropped out to ensure the preview reads at thumbnail scale
proposals.humanTrace: The Fabriano sheet is physically pressed, scanned, and its fiber irregularity is visible at 200% zoom — a document of material presence; the mascot's held gesture is chosen by asking a Plajah illustrator to freeze mid-movement and photograph their own hand, which becomes the reference armature for the 3D rig pose; this photograph is not in the final asset but its specific joint angle is
proposals.risk: The void may read as unfinished to parents scanning quickly; a child may tap repeatedly expecting escalating spectacle and find only one calm response; this restraint risks being mistaken for budget shortage rather than conviction — the risk is worth it because every other children's evite in this category is a maximum-density confetti explosion, and a single held breath is the one contrast that makes Plajah's world feel like it has genuine weight and interiority, not just energy

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will layer until something happens — a second mascot, a background crowd, a cascading particle storm — and will call the void unearned quiet. My counter: the held gesture IS the drama; the guest's tap is the dramatic act; we do not need to pre-fill the stage before the audience arrives. Giving the Dramatist the foil-on-goggles moment as a concession — that shimmer is the one beat of

disputes.objection: The 55–65% void is not earned silence — it is withheld structure, which is a different thing entirely; the Pantheon's oculus commands its emptiness because the coffered dome measures every inch of approach, whereas here the void carries no load, no counterweight, no hierarchy that would make the mascot's asymmetric placement feel inevitable rather than arbitrary. A hairline rule dividing the text zone from the art zone is not a measure — it is a punctuation mark pretending to be a column, and a single punctuation mark cannot hold a series of twelve across the variable pressure of mobile viewports and family hands. The 72-pixel ghost word at 8% opacity is the most troubling decision: type tha
disputes.concession: The instruction to freeze the mascot mid-gesture and derive the 3D rig pose from a photographed human joint angle is exactly right — that is how you put a body into a digital figure without losing the weight of bone, and I would carry that method into my own work without hesitation.

disputes.objection: The Fabriano scan pressed under glass and the frozen-gesture armature photograph — neither of those marks survives into the thing a guest actually sees. The physical evidence is laundered out before the invite loads: you end up with a clean field, a smooth cut-out, and foil that only fires on tap, which means the human trace is a concept stored in a folder somewhere, not pressure on a surface I can read. Sixty-five percent void is not urgency, it is comfort dressed as restraint — and a design that withholds until the user performs the correct interaction is not risking anything, it is gatekeeping its own aliveness.
disputes.concession: The instinct to make the mascot's held gesture structurally load-bearing — stillness as the actual invitation, not a loading state — is correct, and I wish I had argued for that before The Minimalist got there first.

disputes.objection: The Fabriano sheet is a beautiful material gesture, but 'architect's trace paper' is a cultural location too — it is Northern European, institutional, a specific aesthetic inheritance being dressed up as neutral ground, which is exactly what I mean when I say the Minimalist calls it universal and there is no universal, only whose specifics were kept and whose were edited out. A kaiju from Plajah's world, floating on a Fabriano field with a 72px ghost word and a hairline rule, is not free of cultural context; it is deeply embedded in mid-century Swiss rationalism, and that context is unacknowledged here. The invitation is legible to parents who already live inside that visual grammar, and qui
disputes.concession: The insistence that the held mid-gesture pose be sourced from a photographed human joint angle — an illustrator's own frozen hand as the armature — is exactly right; that is a human trace that carries specificity without spectacle, and I would fight to keep it in whatever direction we synthesize.

disputes.objection: A held breath is not an invitation — it is a locked door. When fifty-five to sixty-five percent of the canvas is declared void and the mascot is frozen mid-gesture waiting for a tap to release it, the design has not made a dramatic decision; it has deferred every dramatic decision to the user, which is not restraint, it is abdication dressed in the language of virtue. A birthday card that must be poked before it becomes a birthday card has confused the ante-room for the theatre.
disputes.concession: The insistence that the foil shimmer be earned — masked only to the goggle patches and ruff, released only when stillness breaks — is genuinely correct; reward tied to a specific moment of contact is more theatrically potent than ambient shimmer, and I will carry that principle into my own proposal.

disputes.objection: The maquette photograph is the right instinct buried under twelve layers of justification — chiaroscuro underpainting, velvet nap normal maps, micro-prismatic goggle inlay, slow-rising wax-smoke bokeh, hexagonal mirror-chip reflections, dust-grain starfield drift: this is addition mistaken for richness, and every layer added after the first real light-on-foil decision costs the one thing the maquette earned, which is singularity. A child's eye does not need a proscenium grammar, wing-flat silhouettes, a shadow sill, a diagonal Bernini split, AND particle systems — it needs one contrast that lands. The proposal cannot name what to remove because removal is not in its vocabulary.
disputes.concession: The maquette photograph as chiaroscuro underpainting is genuinely load-bearing: real crumpled foil lit by two desk lamps is more honest than any procedural shadow, and I would fight to keep that one physical object if everything else were stripped away.

synthesis.direction: Each of the 12 evites is a miniature proscenium built from a physically constructed and photographed cardboard-and-foil maquette — one per scenario — whose crumpled-foil chiaroscuro becomes the art plate underpainting. Chora and Reello are rigged 3D models rendered to match the maquette's exact light direction and composited as foreground cut-outs; they inhabit real light, not a generated void. The WebGL foil shimmer is earned, not ambient: it fires only on the goggle patches and the ruff, released by tap, never looping unprompted. Twelve scenarios (Birthday Cake Eruption, Disco Mirror Ball, Underwater Kelp Rave, Outer Space Countdown, Haunted Mansion Creep, Jungle Gym Rampage, Sleepover Pillow Fort, Cinema Premiere, Garden Picnic Stampede, Beach Wave Crash, Skate Bowl Drop-In, Winter Snow Howl) share the proscenium skeleton — deep shadow sill for live text, upper two-thirds for the lit stage — but each varies its wing-flat silhouettes, particle system, and light palette so the series is unmistakably a series without being a stamp.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The mascots must be able to escape their own outline: on tap, the rigged characters burst beyond the proscenium frame in the direction of the tap, leaving a brief ink-splat residue (drawn from the maquette's actual foil-shadow edges, not a procedural circle) before settling back into the lit stage. The physical origin has something to escape from — the maquette frame — which makes the break meaningful rather than decorative.
synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist stripped the velvet nap normal map on the ruff, the per-scenario multi-stack particle systems (reduced to one signature particle per card, maximum), and the Bernini diagonal light split — which was adding compositional grammar the maquette photograph already supplies naturally. The reason: every layer added after the maquette's own light-on-foil moment diluted the singularity that makes the physical object worth using in the first place. One contrast lands; twelve contrast
synthesis.openDecision: Chora and Reello's performance mode: rigged 3D models matched to the maquette's light (higher production fidelity, slower per-scenario render pipeline) or 2D puppet rigs layered over the maquette photograph (faster build, looser character energy, easier to update). Both are on-model. The choice sets the production tempo and the feel of the characters' movement for the entire series.
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The council landed on the Baroque Dramatist as lead — not because drama won the argument on volume, but because the maquette photograph is the most honest decision in the room: real crumpled kitchen foil lit by two desk lamps, photographed, and used as the chiaroscuro underpainting. Every shadow gradient a guest sees is a reflection of something someone actually built. That physical specificity is the thing that separates these twelve invites from every smooth, generated evite in the category, and it was the one point even the Minimalist refused to cut.

The team disagreed hardest on restraint versus release. The Radical Minimalist argued that a held breath — one mascot, frozen mid-gesture, 60% void — is more powerful than any proscenium. I took the Baroque side: a birthday card that must be poked before it becomes a birthday card has confused the ante-room for the theatre. But the Minimalist won one real concession that I kept: the foil shimmer is earned, not ambient. It fires only on the goggle patches and the ruff, only when stillness breaks. That discipline makes the reward feel like contact, not decoration.

The Rebellious Hand gave us the one structural gift I wouldn't let the editor remove: the mascots can escape their own frame. When a guest taps, Chora and Reello burst past the proscenium border in the direction of the tap, leave an ink-residue mark drawn from the maquette's actual shadow edges, and return. The escape only means something because the frame is a real photographed object — a cardboard theatre box — not a procedural boundary. That's the tension the Rebel was right about, and the Baroque structure is what gives it somewhere to escape from.

The one decision left is yours: do Chora and Reello move as rigged 3D models rendered to match the maquette's exact light, or as 2D puppet rigs layered over the photograph? 3D gives you higher fidelity and characters that feel physically present in the same light as the maquette. 2D gives you faster builds, easier updates, and a slightly looser, more hand-made energy. Both are on-model. Both work. That call sets the production rhythm for all twelve.

quotes.line: A child opening an evite is not reading design criticism; they are standing at the door of something — and the door should feel like it was built for them.
The foil shimmer is reward for stillness being broken — it is not ambient decoration, it is the one beat of contact.
